extracted.intended_audience: legal scholars, practitioners, and Penn State law students considering submission to the Penn State Law Review
extracted.subtask_short: publishing in penn state law review
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the Penn State Law Review's scope, the types of work it publishes, and basic selection/publication practices for prospective authors and student commentators. Targets those considering submitting articles or writing student comments for this specific journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: General-interest scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Penn State Law Review is the flagship publication of Penn State Law. As a general-interest journal, the Penn State Law Review publishes in the broad range of legal scholarship and does not limit submissions by any specific topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied guidance: prospective authors may submit on any legal topic since the journal does not restrict subject matter. No further topical restrictions or prioritizations are specified on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of works published
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, each issue includes several legal articles and comments. The articles are written by legal scholars and practitioners, and the comments are written by Penn State law students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes permitted author types by piece type: articles (scholars/practitioners) vs. comments (Penn State law students). Implies that student comments are the student-authored component; no submission procedure details are provided here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process (stringent evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every year, as part of a stringent selection process, the journal evaluates a host of submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates competitive/rigorous selection but provides no scoring criteria, deadlines, length limits, or procedural details on this page. Authors should expect competitive review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Law Review publishes three print issues per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical information about cadence: submissions are considered for triannual print issues. No detail about online-first publication or symposium issues is given on this page.
